LESSON: SUBTRACTION (8

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: MATHEMATICS
Strand: Numbers
Topic 1.3: Subtraction (8

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello learner! Today we will learn about Subtraction (8. Read, look at the pictures, practise, then try the revision quiz.

SECTION 2: LEARN

Today, we are going to subtract capacity involving litres. In this lesson, we will require the following, counting sticks, Pieces of thread, Writing material and a rubber. Welcome to Mathematics Lesson for Grade four. Today, we shall do subtraction of capacity in litres. Yes, Learner. We shall subtract capacity in Litres. Before that, let us remind ourselves how to subtract using sticks similar to what we learned in grade three. We are going to remind ourselves how to subtract using sticks similar to what we learned in grade three. The first example. If we had to subtract 12 from 27 Learner, we first need to count 27 loose sticks. Yes. We need to count 27 loose sticks. With 27 Sticks, We have two bundles of 10 and Seven loose Sticks. Good job. Subtracting 12 means that we subtract two from the seven loose sticks, leaving us with five at the ones place value. Remember, We took away two sticks from the seven loose sticks, leaving us with the five news sticks at the ones place value. Now, at Tens Place Value, we subtract one bundle of sticks from the two bundle of sticks, leaving us with one bundle of sticks. Learner, What is your final answer?

Good. our answer is 15. Our second example. Let us now subtract 19 litres from 32 litres. Let us now subtract 19 litres from 32 litres. Count 32 sticks. Tie them into bundles of 10. Tie them into bundles of 10. How many bundles of 10 do we have? How many bundles of 10 do we have? We have three bundles of 10. And how many lose sticks are we left with? Yes, we have 2 loose Sticks. Three bundles of sticks and two sticks is equal to thirty two sticks. Let us now subtract 19 from 32, and we first start with the ones place value. Learner, do you notice that we cannot subtract 9 from 2? This means that we regroup one tens from three to nine and leave 2 at Tens. One tens has 10 ones. Yes, One tens has 10 ones. 10 Ones added to 2 loose sticks is equal to 12. Ten added to 2 loose sticks is equal to 12. Subtracting ten from 12 leaves us with three at ones place value. Learner, at the Tens place value, we have 2 ten bundles of sticks. We subtract one bundle and we are left with One 10 bundles of stick. Learner, what then is our final answer? Yes, Thirteen is our answer. But since we are doing subtraction of litres, let us make sure we write the initial “l”. The initial “l” is in small letter. And this has to be at the end of our answer. Yes, we must write the initial “l” or small letter l to mean Litres. This then means that our answer is 13 litres or in return form 13l. small l.

Learner, you can also write the word in full, as in 13 Litres. L. i. t. r. e. s. The following activity will help us understand more on how to subtract capacity in litres. Learner, I will read the number story and you will write the substraction story, then work it out. A. Godana’s family tank had two thousand nine hundred and fifty eight litres of water. In one week, the family used eight hundred and thirty nine litres of water. What amount of water in litres remained in the tank? I will repeat. A. Godana’s family tank had two thousand nine hundred and fifty eight litres of water. In one week, the family used eight hundred and thirty nine litres of water. What amount of water in litres remained in the tank? What was the amount of water in litres that remained in the tank? B. A school tank had seven thousand five hundred and thirty five litres of water. A school tank had seven thousand five hundred and thirty five litres of water. Learners used three thousand two hundred and twenty nine litres of water for cleaning. Learners used three thousand two hundred and twenty nine litres of water for cleaning. How many litres of water remained in the tank? How many litres of water remained in the tank? I will repeat. A school tank had seven thousand five hundred and thirty five litres of water. Learners used three thousand two hundred and twenty nine litres of water for cleaning. How many litres of water remained in the tank?

C. A factory processed 10, 000 litres of juice. A factory processed 10, 000 litres of juice. A trader bought five thousand six hundred litres of juice. A trader bought five thousand six hundred litres of juice. How many litres of juice remained? How many litres of juice remained? I will repeat. A factory processed 10, 000 litres of juice. A trader bought five thousand six hundred litres of juice. How many litres of juice remained? Learner, kindly share your answers with your parents, guardians or friends. I hope you enjoyed the lesson, stay safe and keep observing hygiene. Your radio teacher was Scholah Mkadho. This program was written and produced by the It was recorded by Johnson Mwangi for the Institute of Curriculum Development. Until next time, Goodbye.

SECTION 3: TRY THIS

1. Look again at the examples or pictures above.
2. Tell a parent or friend what Subtraction (8 means, using your own words.
3. Copy one example into your exercise book and change it to fit your school or home.
4. Underline three new words and find out what they mean.

SECTION 4: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Subtraction (8.
2. Complete any “Work to do” items shown in the pupil book pages above.
3. Create three of your own practice questions on this topic.
4. Answer the Revision Quiz. Check Answers only after finishing.

SECTION 5: REMEMBER

1. Topic: Subtraction (8
2. Subject: MATHEMATICS
